assertions.name: crossing_count_is_exactly_twelve_A_minus_one
assertions.unit: exact match on all six N=Z nuclei
assertions.source: n_strands = 3A and the construction places 4 crossings per strand, so crossings = 4*n_strands - 1 = 12A - 1: affine in A, extensive BY CONSTRUCTION

assertions.name: neither_ratio_is_constant
assertions.unit: smaller of the two fractional spreads

description: Tests the prediction from the non-abelian Stokes audit that the surface coefficient a_S tracks a singularity count. The canonical braid's crossing count is 12*A - 1 EXACTLY on all six N=Z nuclei (= 4*n_strands - 1), hence affine in A and extensive by construction. A surface term scales as A^(2/3), and (12m^3-1)/m^2 = 12m - 1/m^2 is strictly monotone, so no constant coefficient works at even two mass numbers (QOU.Mass.AffineCountIsNotASurfaceTerm). Scope-(b) for that form only. The useful half: Yekutieli's bad set stratifies a 2-cell structure and a braid WORD is 1-dimensional, so the route needs the spanning surface, which the framework does not construct.

ratio_spreads.note: recorded for completeness; the ARGUMENT is the monotonicity theorem, not these numbers -- they would not become evidence if they happened to be closer

what_the_route_needs_instead.why_untestable_here: Yekutieli's bad set stratifies a 2-dimensional cell structure (a kite: 1-simplex + 2-simplex); a braid WORD is 1-dimensional and has no 2-cell structure to stratify
what_the_route_needs_instead.what_would_test_it: the spanning surface -- Seifert genus, boundary components, or a genuine 2-cell decomposition -- which the framework does not presently construct
what_the_route_needs_instead.scope: (b) for 'crossing count times a constant' via the proved monotonicity invariant; (a) for any wider claim about crossings
